backlog.title: Introduction To FP8 Formats: Part 1
backlog.summary:
The rationale behind 8-bit floating-point data formats, their ecosystem momentum, and hardware support.
The post Introduction To FP8 Formats: Part 1 appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The rationale behind 8-bit floating-point data formats, their ecosystem momentum, and hardware support.
The industry is moving from high-precision formats (FP32, FP16, BF16) to lower-precision data types for Machine Learning (ML) inference and training.
In cloud and data center environments, lower-precision data types deliver higher throughput by packing more compute per cycle from the same platform.
On edge and mobile devices, smaller formats reduce model size, memory footprint and bandwidth, which directly affects power consumption and latency.
Arm, Intel, and NVIDIA published an OCP 8-bit Floating Point Specification (OFP8).

The post The Semiconductor Singularity: When AI Starts Accelerating The Silicon That Accelerates AI appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Use evidence from silicon to improve the tools and decisions that create the next generation of hardware.
AI is entering the inner loop of semiconductor engineering by reducing the effort required to develop software, operate software tools and carry out engineering analysis.
Ray Kurzweil described the broader pattern as the Law of Accelerating Returns: accumulated technical capability helps create the next computing paradigm.
In my recent white paper, The semiconductor singularity: Accelerating IC innovation with AI, I applied that idea to semiconductor engineering.
Better computing improves the tools used to design and manufacture semiconductors, and those tools help create the next generation of computing.

backlog.title: Beyond Bandwidth: AI Inference Is Reshaping The Memory Wall

The post Beyond Bandwidth: AI Inference Is Reshaping The Memory Wall appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Longer contexts, higher concurrency, multimodal models, and AI agents will continue changing where memory pressure appears.
AI infrastructure has spent the past several years in a race for compute.
More accelerators, larger heterogeneous clusters, and higher peak performance have enabled increasingly capable models.
As AI moves into large-scale deployment, infrastructure must support more users, larger models, longer context windows, and more complex applications.
Performance still matters, but so do latency, power, utilization, predictability, and cost per inference.

backlog.title: Building AI that can work across the enterprise
backlog.summary: For years, enterprises have approached AI as a series of discrete experiments. Now, as AI agents begin to move into the workflows that run the business, that model is starting to look inadequate. Organizations moving from isolated pilots toward AI agents and autonomous workflows are confronting a deeper challenge: rethinking how data, business processes, governance,…
bullets: Enterprises are moving away from isolated AI pilots toward integrated 'digital coworker' models, requiring a fundamental shift in data infrastructure and governance.

Experts emphasize that AI deployment in mission-critical areas like supply chains requires near-perfect accuracy, as the '80% success' threshold acceptable in experimental phases is insufficient for operations.
Scalability is the primary hurdle for enterprise AI; projects that cannot be replicated across business units are categorized as failed experiments rather than strategic assets.
Proactive governance is essential to avoid a 'risk backlog,' as the absence of clear access controls and monitoring will eventually force disruptive audits and operational halts.

backlog.title: IP Integration Challenges Evolve
backlog.summary:
Integration challenges are growing more complex, but the problem is well understood and solutions are emerging.
The post IP Integration Challenges Evolve appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Integration challenges are growing more complex, but the problem is well understood and solutions are emerging.

Key Takeaways:
IP integration is not the most glamorous task in semiconductor design, but it often is one of the most troublesome.
At the intersection of block-level verification and system-level interactions, bugs are often very difficult to find.
The creation of the Virtual Socket Interface Alliance (VSIA) in 1996 was, for many, the first time the notion of designing a system by integrating third-party IP blocks became a reality.
Its charter was to unify and standardize the way IP was constructed, verified, delivered, and supported.

backlog.title: Self-Supervised Virtual Metrology For CMP MRR Prediction (SUTD, A*STAR, NUS)
backlog.summary:
Researchers at Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD), A*STAR, and National University of Singapore (NUS) published “Self-Supervised Attention-Based Virtual Metrology for CMP MRR Prediction.” Excerpt “In this paper, we propose Global Regression Pretraining (GREP), a self-supervised, attention-based framework for CMP* MRR prediction. GREP learns temporal representations from unlabeled sensor signals through global proxy-target regression,... » read more
The post Self-Supervised Virtual Metrology For CMP MRR Prediction (SUTD, A*STAR, NUS) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers have developed Global Regression Pretraining (GREP), a self-supervised framework designed to predict Material Removal Rate (MRR) in chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) processes.
The framework utilizes attention-based mechanisms to learn temporal representations from unlabeled sensor signals, significantly reducing the reliance on large labeled datasets.
GREP demonstrates robustness against common manufacturing challenges, including sensor noise, limited labeled data availability, and temporal process drift.

backlog.title: More autonomy, fewer NDAs: Volunteers have new requests for brain implant trials
backlog.summary: Scientists have been working on ways to decode brain activity for decades. Teams have developed brain implants that can be used to control robotic limbs and computers, and even to “speak.” The people who volunteer for trials of those devices play a vital role in that research, and they ought to be recognized for their…
bullets: Participants in brain-computer interface (BCI) clinical trials are advocating for new ethical guidelines to ensure greater autonomy and access to their own neural data.
The BCI Pioneers Coalition is pushing back against restrictive non-disclosure agreements and seeking formal recognition for the long-term physical and intellectual contributions of trial volunteers.
Legal and neuroethics experts argue that BCI trials require unique ethical frameworks because they involve permanent, long-term integration of hardware into the human brain.

backlog.title: What Is Acoustic Micro Imaging? A Quick Guide To This Inspection Process
backlog.summary:
Obtaining clear images of gaps and delaminations in advanced packages.
The post What Is Acoustic Micro Imaging? A Quick Guide To This Inspection Process appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Acoustic Micro Imaging (AMI) utilizes high-frequency ultrasound to detect internal defects like delaminations and air gaps in advanced semiconductor packages.
The technology relies on transducers to convert electrical pulses into mechanical waves, which cannot travel through air, allowing for the precise identification of structural voids.
While non-destructive, AMI is increasingly critical for maintaining high yields and reliability as package complexity and feature density continue to scale.

backlog.title: Can AI Agents Really Shift Chip Design Left?
backlog.summary:
Agentic AI promises to automate more of the chip flow, but integration with EDA tools and capturing decades of engineering expertise are non-trivial.
The post Can AI Agents Really Shift Chip Design Left? appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Agentic AI is poised to transform chip design methodologies, potentially mirroring the industry-wide adoption of UVM, though the integration of disparate agents into a cohesive workflow remains an unsolved challenge.

Industry experts warn that many AI startups lack the necessary field experience to solve real-world design problems, leading major chipmakers to prioritize building proprietary, in-house AI solutions.
There is potential for AI to replace traditional simulation languages like UVM with synthesizable SystemVerilog, which could significantly accelerate emulation speeds and reduce software overhead.

The shift toward AI-driven design raises critical concerns regarding the protection of proprietary design data and the difficulty of codifying decades of institutional engineering expertise into automated models.

backlog.title: Blog Review: Nov. 18
backlog.summary:
PCIe and trust; rack-scale co-design; heterogeneous scaling; AI data center primer; on-device balancing; EU semi trends.
The post Blog Review: Nov. 18 appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Data center architecture is shifting toward extreme co-design, where silicon, memory, power, and cooling are integrated as a single system to meet the thermal and performance demands of AI workloads.
Heterogeneous scaling and 3D-IC technologies are replacing monolithic designs, necessitating new approaches to managing complexity in chiplet-based architectures.

Memory hierarchy optimization is becoming critical as multimodal models and AI agents create unpredictable memory pressure, requiring designers to right-size systems based on specific data reuse patterns.
Security concerns are mounting as sensitive models and cryptographic keys increasingly traverse PCIe links, prompting a focus on establishing hardware-level trust in interconnected systems.

backlog.title: The AI Hype Index: AI is everywhere
backlog.summary: Like a nasty rash, AI seems to spread everywhere. Google crams AI Overviews down your throat even though it costs the company billions of dollars in lost ad revenue. Leave your apartment, and you might pass two people heaving an AI-powered humanoid robot up the stairs to clean someone’s rooms. Go to the supermarket, and…
bullets: The current AI landscape is characterized by aggressive integration across consumer products, often at the expense of corporate profitability, such as Google's costly AI Overviews.
Market saturation has led to a 'hype cycle' where AI is being forced into hardware and media, creating a user experience that many perceive as intrusive or unoptimized.

Critical analysis suggests that despite the pervasive marketing, current Large Language Models (LLMs) still lack true reasoning capabilities, casting doubt on the sustainability of the current AGI-focused investment narrative.
